claims.statement: From 2026, covered importers above the threshold must report embedded emissions and surrender purchased CBAM certificates; certificate cash cost is a current measurable exposure.
The authorised CBAM declarant buys certificates, making import finance, customs or sustainability leadership a plausible budget owner.

A direct importer workflow-integration and data-processing agreement can make recurring access to importer-controlled records contractible, while the launch service can use customer-uploaded records and public defaults without depending on supplier or verifier data; no such agreement is currently signed.
Pricing, acquisition cost, implementation effort, contribution margin, renewal and customer savings remain unvalidated, and a low-priced direct substitute constrains achievable pricing.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: CFO or treasury lead at a covered importer, with customs leadership as operational sponsor
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: The service is sold as an independent pre-purchase treasury control with a documented exposure register and variance review that can operate beside any ERP; this reduces integration lock-in but does not prevent incumbents from copying or bundling it.
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The prospective business would directly own importer service contracts and billing relationships; no customer contract is currently signed.
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Founder-led targeted outbound to importers above the threshold, followed only by nonexclusive broker or adviser referrals under written referral agreements; no referral channel is currently validated.

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Unvalidated planning range: 4,000-12,000 PLN per customer using narrow account lists and remote sales; abandon or reprice if observed CAC exceeds first-year contribution profit.
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Proposed 50% setup fee at signing, 50% at delivery, then quarterly retainers prepaid; actual payment terms and collection time are unknown.
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unvalidated target: 45-65% on setup work and 60-75% on quarterly retainers after analyst review, support and specialist costs; no cohort evidence exists.
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Planning assumption: 12-25 analyst hours for initial mapping and 3-8 hours per quarterly refresh, plus customer support; automate only after paid repetitions establish stable inputs.
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Planning allowance: 6,000-12,000 PLN monthly at early scale for legal, security, insurance and periodic carbon-method review; accredited verification remains outside scope and is paid directly by the importer.
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Fixed-fee implementation plus prepaid quarterly treasury-control retainer, priced by declarant entity and shipment-data complexity rather than supplier-data volume.
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Analyst QA, secure file handling, customer support and occasional independent methodology review; verifier fees and supplier evidence collection are excluded from the service.

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: SAP, customs suites and low-priced CBAM vendors can bundle dashboards and forecasting or undercut software pricing. Defensibility rests on a lightweight independent treasury-control engagement, faster deployment and documented variance reviews, not exclusive data or protected functionality.
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Importer purchases and surrenders CBAM certificates; the service measures forecast-to-actual certificate cash variance and the cost of procurement scenarios using importer-provided records and official defaults where verified supplier data is unavailable.
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: A covered importer needs an auditable certificate budget before procurement or treasury approval, or experiences a material forecast variance.
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Each prepaid quarterly exposure refresh and annual workflow-integration renewal, subject to demonstrated use and willingness to pay.

contrary_evidence: The 50-tonne threshold removes many small importers from the principal compliance-driven market.
Carbon Glance offers overlapping tracking, projections, procurement and supplier tools for €2,500 per year.
SAP is bundling end-to-end CBAM data, calculation, accounting, reporting and planned cash-impact forecasting.
Essential actual-emissions and verification inputs remain controlled by importers, suppliers and accredited verifiers.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed direct workflow-integration and data-processing agreement requiring the importer to provide defined customs and procurement extracts, designate the exposure register as a quarterly treasury-control input, permit processing for the engagement, and pay prepaid quarterly fees; it is unsigned and grants no present rights.
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Deliver a one-off, prepaid exposure diagnostic from customer-uploaded shipment records and public certificate prices/default values without ERP integration, supplier data or verifier outputs; if the importer will not provide even those records, do not launch for that account.
critical_control_point.current_owner: Importers currently own the source records and treasury process; suppliers and accredited verifiers retain control of actual-emissions evidence and assurance outputs. The prospective business currently owns no signed workflow position.
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The prospective business would directly own importer service contracts and billing relationships; no customer contract is currently signed.
critical_control_point.duration: Proposed 12-month agreement with quarterly prepaid work orders; duration remains unestablished until signature.
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No existing importer, supplier, broker or verifier rights are established; the proposed agreement is an acquisition path, not present access.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: The founder controls whether to offer and deliver the public-default diagnostic and would control the exposure-register process and software templates; each importer controls whether to sign and supply its records.
critical_control_point.renewal: Proposed annual renewal with quarterly service confirmation; renewal behavior is unvalidated.
critical_control_point.subject: Contracted importer treasury exposure-register workflow using importer-provided records and a public-default fallback

economics.acquisition_route: Sell a prepaid, fixed-scope exposure-register implementation directly to narrowly targeted covered importers; convert only customers that use the register in treasury decisions to prepaid quarterly retainers, and add nonexclusive referral agreements after direct-sales economics are observed.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario: reach 40 retained customers at an average 48,000 PLN annual retainer plus 20 implementations at 12,000 PLN, producing 2.16M PLN annual revenue. At 25% owner earnings and a 3x revenue valuation, a 70% founder stake could exceed 4.5M PLN in business equity, with reinvested earnings potentially taking founder net worth above 5M PLN in roughly years 7-10. This fails if retention, delivery leverage, pricing or acquisition economics do not hold.
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly during validation, capped by fixed-scope implementations; contract analyst QA only after prepaid demand and standardized delivery are observed.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Implementation and retainer revenue less analyst QA, support, secure data handling and specialist review; target ranges are hypotheses until paid delivery data exists.
economics.payback: Require each implementation to document a forecast variance, avoided manual effort or procurement decision worth at least the fee; no 1-3% certificate saving is assumed, and payback remains unproven.
economics.pricing: Proposed 10,000-18,000 PLN prepaid implementation and 9,000-15,000 PLN prepaid quarterly retainer; test against the €2,500 annual substitute and reduce scope rather than claim premium willingness.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Quarterly price changes, shipment updates and annual declarations create repeat work, but renewal is conditional on the exposure register being used in treasury approval and remains unvalidated.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable exposure-register templates, importer-specific variance histories and permissioned workflow learning; no exclusive regulatory-data moat is assumed.
fingerprint.customer: EU mid-market importers of steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity or hydrogen.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Direct account-based importer sales first; nonexclusive written broker or adviser referrals only after direct acquisition economics are measured.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Prepaid exposure-register implementation plus quarterly productized treasury-control service using importer-provided records and public-default fallback.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Importer pays subscription against certificate purchase and surrender events.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Covered import volume crosses threshold or treasury exposure becomes material.

founder_fit: Fixed-scope remote delivery can remain compatible with part-time availability during validation
Prepaid diagnostics limit initial capital exposure and create observable delivery economics

redesign.economic_effect: Replaces speculative high-priced SaaS and uncontrolled supplier-data dependence with a directly contracted, prepaid treasury-control service that can launch on importer-uploaded records and public defaults. Capital need and onboarding effort fall, verifier and supplier costs move outside scope, and cash conversion improves through prepayment; margins and scale potential are lower and remain unvalidated until paid implementations establish CAC, labor, retention and price tolerance.

risks: No importer has signed the proposed workflow-integration agreement or paid for the redesigned service.
The low-priced substitute and SAP bundling may cap price or eliminate demand for an independent treasury-control layer.
Customer-uploaded records and public defaults may produce insufficient decision value to support quarterly retention.
Enterprise trust, security review and sales cycles may exceed the founder's part-time capacity.
Regulatory or methodology errors create liability; the service must not represent itself as accredited verification.

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: prepaid cbam treasury exposure register implementation and quarterly control service
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: proposed direct importer agreement placing an exposure register in quarterly treasury approval with a no integration public default fallback
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: importer signature provision of defined records and recurring use of the exposure register in treasury decisions

structure.control_point: Directly contracted quarterly exposure register used in importer treasury approval
structure.critical_dependency: Importer adoption and provision of defined customs and procurement extracts; supplier and verifier data are optional rather than launch-critical

thesis: Acquire a contractible position in the importer's recurring treasury-control workflow and deliver useful CBAM cash-variance decisions from defined importer records and public defaults, without making supplier evidence or accredited verification a launch dependency.
title: CBAM Treasury Exposure Register
uncertainties: Whether covered importers will sign the proposed workflow-integration terms and pay the implementation or quarterly fees
Observed direct-sales CAC, sales cycle, delivery hours, security burden, contribution margin and renewal
Whether public-default and importer-record analysis creates sufficient incremental value beside €2,500 software and bundled ERP tools
Whether the founder can standardize delivery enough to reach the modeled customer count within part-time constraints
